claims.claim: The 2026 year-end tax preview is available from Oct 28 to Dec 18, 2026 through Hometax's Convenient Year-end Settlement menu.
The tool uses expected annual income, Jan-Sep card use and user-entered expected Oct-Dec spending/expenses to estimate tax, card deduction effects and personalized deduction information.
The preview is an estimate, not a confirmed refund; actual outcomes can differ with actual income/spending and final supporting records.

The official 2026 guide says the descendant income requirement for education expense credits is removed and qualifying arts/sports tuition for children under 9 or in grade 2 or lower may qualify; it also lists a 40% hometown donation credit for the portion over 100,000 to 200,000 KRW and generally 15% for the excess over 200,000 KRW. Personal eligibility conditions still apply.

sources.title: 13월의 월급, 나는 얼마나 받을까?
sources.body: Korea Policy Briefing/official tax guide. 2026 preview opens Oct 28-Dec 18. Hometax path: 장려금·연말정산·기부금 > 편리한 연말정산 > 연말정산 미리보기. Steps: estimate annual pay, review Jan-Sep card spending and enter Oct-Dec expected spending, amend expected deduction categories, view estimated tax and three-year trends. Preview is not a final amount. Education credit: descendant income requirement removed; qualifying arts/sports tuition for children under 9 or in grade 2 or lower may qualify. Hometown donation credit: 40% for amount over 100,000 KRW up to 200,000 KRW, 15% for the excess over 200,000 KRW generally. Personal statutory eligibility applies.

sources.body: National Tax Service's 2025-11-05 notice for previous-year preview: service uses Jan-Sep card usage and prior filed deductions to estimate tax; users can consider year-end spending/saving; illustrative precedent, not this year's date.

sources.title: 국세청 연말정산 종합 안내
sources.body: National Tax Service official 2025 year-end settlement guide and individual eligibility/filing reference. This covers statutory qualification and filing details; the official Korea Policy Briefing guide is the source for the Oct 28-Dec 18 preview window and 2026 deduction changes.

cannotSay: The preview does not guarantee a refund or establish a final tax liability.
Do not give individualized tax advice or imply every deduction fits every household.
Use the official opening window Oct 28-Dec 18, not an assumed annual date.
